title: Commitment Sway Controller and Isolation Lattice - PRD (rough)
body:
Purpose: sketch a controller that balances committed dedicated capacity against transient demand using a lightweight crediting model we call the "Commitment Sway Controller" (CSC) and an operational pattern we call the "isolation lattice". This doc is a pragmatic PRD + ops notes: prioritized behaviors, API hooks, telemetry, failure modes, and rollout plan. Draft - rough thinking, lots of TODOs and open questions.

Problem statement:
- Customers want predictable throughput from Dedicated while still getting cost-effective handling of occasional spikes without manual reserve changes.
- Current reserved pools are binary: reserved or not. Bursting is ad-hoc and can cause noisy-neighbor effects.
- Teams need a graduated set of guarantees (soft isolation) and fast transient elasticity while preserving SLOs for paying customers.

Design goals (what success looks like):
1) Predictable SLOs for committed tenants: 95th/99th latency and throughput guarantees within their committed window.
2) Transient surge handling: allow short-lived spikes to exceed commitment automatically within bounded economic and performance limits.
3) Controlled isolation: prevent single-tenant surges from degrading others beyond defined soft-limits.
4) Transparent economics: clear metrics and billing signals for when surges consume non-committed compute.
5) Operational simplicity: on-call, troubleshooting paths, and a reversible rollout.

High-level concept:
- Commitment Sway Controller (CSC): an orchestrator that manages per-tenant allocations across a continuous space (not discrete slots). Each tenant has: committed_capacity (RPS or tokens/min), sway_budget (short-window credit they can borrow), and fidelity_profile (latency vs. cost tier).
- Isolation lattice: a multi-dimensional enforcement fabric: commit-band (hard), sway-band (soft, metered), and opportunistic-band (best-effort, preemptible). Requests are routed into bands based on tenant state and controller signals.

Behavioral rules (early draft):
- Normal: tenant consumes from commit-band up to committed_capacity. All SLO metrics logged to tenant dashboard.
- Surge: transient traffic above committed_capacity consumes sway_budget first (fast), then opportunistic-band if available. Sway usage increments a metered counter used for billing and capacity reconciliation.
- Depletion: if sway_budget exhausted, requests are subject to one of: queued short-term, best-effort degraded responses, degrade-to-lighter-model, or rate-limited depending on tenant policy. These are configurable per-account.
- Preemption: opportunistic-band resources may be reclaimed by other tenants or autoscaler activities; reclaim events are graceful with eviction callbacks.

Controller algorithm (informal pseudocode):
1) Continuously collect per-tenant metrics: RPS, concurrency, queue latency, token-per-request estimate, kv-cache hit ratio, recent sway_usage.
2) Forecast short-window delta via EWMA and a burstiness score.
3) Allocate commit_band demand deterministically for committed_capacity.
4) If observed demand > commit_band, allow up to sway_budget * multiplier (multiplier depends on fidelity_profile) into sway-band and mark usage.
5) If cluster headroom low, reduce multiplier across tenants by priority and recent usage.

Credit accounting model (sweep-shelf):
- sway_budget: replenishes slowly (e.g., daily) up to a configured cap. It is charged at a higher per-token premium when consumed.
- surge_credit: instantaneous credit pool drawn from unused commit_band in other tenants (if policy allows cross-tenant spillover). This is optional and requires customer opt-in.
- reconciliation: daily batch reconciles sway consumption into billing/invoice line items and feeds the Optimize recommender for capacity adjustments.

API and UX surface (for Console + API):
- Tenant config fields: committed_capacity, sway_budget_cap, sway_replenish_rate, fidelity_profile (latency-weighted|cost-weighted), surge_opt_in: [none|spillover|peer-lend].
- Observable metrics: current_band (commit|sway|opportunistic), active_sway_usage, daily_sway_consumed, predicted_next_1m_burst, blocked_requests_count, degrade_actions_count.
- Alerts: sway_budget_low, sustained_sway_>x%_for_10m, cross-tenant_reclamation_event, preemption_rate_high.

Operational runbooks (first pass):
- Emergency throttle: ops can flip tenant to strict isolation (hard-cut) for immediate protection. This is a manual override with audit log.
- Rollback plan: enable CSC in monitoring-only mode (no enforcement) -> opt-in beta groups -> open to all with default conservative multipliers -> enable full enforcement.
- Incident triage: trace requestID -> band assignment -> token accounting -> model size/compute path to determine if degradation due to kv-cache eviction or kernel mismatch.

Telemetry + SLOs:
- Per-tenant: P50/P95/P99 latency for commit-band vs sway-band, throughput delivered vs committed, % requests served from opportunistic.
- Cluster: headroom percentage, preemption events/min, cross-tenant spillover volume.
- Alerting thresholds: configured for product ops initially at sustained sway > 30% of cluster headroom for 5m.

Billing implications and UX for customers:
- Sway consumption shows in console as "Burst usage" with clear per-token premium and projected charge if trend continues.
- Recommend capacity when sustained sway > 20% of committed for 6 hours. Recommendation flow: one-click increase, schedule, or start a trial of fractional commitment.

Edge cases and failure modes:
- Prediction failure: rapid fan-out (e.g., viral event) can exhaust sway and opportunistic bands quickly. Mitigation: conservative default multipliers and per-tenant cap on simultaneous active sway flows.
- Billing spikes: need throttle for billing events; show estimated cost and an explicit confirmation before exceeding soft monetary thresholds.
- Preemption thrash: if opportunistic resources constantly reclaimed, spike requests see high latency. Add hysteresis and soft-backoff on reclaim cycles.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
1) How to set default multipliers for new accounts? Conservative but still useful for small spikes. 2) Cross-tenant spillover is powerful but introduces accounting complexity and privacy/tenant trust issues. Opt-in only? opt-out? 3) How fine-grained should sway_budget be (tokens vs request-count vs compute-seconds)? Tokens are model-aware but require reliable token estimates. 4) API contract for degrade actions: do we expose structured reasons in responses? (helpful for client UX) 5) Interaction with Dedicated autoscaling: if Dedicated autoscaler spins up more machines, do we expand sway budgets or prefer commit-band scaling?

Telemetry schema (sample fields):
- tenant_id, timestamp, band, request_id, model_id, tokens_estimated, tokens_charged, latency_ms, outcome (ok|degraded|dropped), sway_credit_drawn

Rollout plan (milestones):
- Feb 2025: prototype CSC in staging with two beta tenants. Monitoring-only mode for 2 weeks.
- Mar 2025: enable enforcement for beta tenants; show burst billing in console. Gather ops and billing signals.
- Apr 2025: expand to 20% of traffic, add recommendation flow in Console.
- May 2025: GA with conservative defaults and full docs.

Backward compatibility and migration notes:
- Existing dedicated customers default to sway_budget=0 unless they opt into beta. We will provide a simple toggle in Console to opt-in and a migration audit log.
- For customers using older billing contracts, special handling required; coordinate with finance.

Operational costs and capacity modeling notes (for Finance/Capacity planning):
- Expect surge premium revenue but also higher egress of opportunistic compute. Need to model tail utilization and incremental GPU hours.
- Conservative estimate: if 10% of tenants use sway at 15% of committed on average, cluster utilization increases by ~1.5% but with variance.

Appendix - example flows:
1) Small SaaS app: committed 100k tokens/day, sudden campaign creates 3x spike for 20 minutes. CSC allows sway-budget draw and charges premium. Console shows a pop-up tip: "Consider 2x commit during sales hours".
2) Enterprise bank (opted for no spillover): gets surge - after sway exhausted, responses are queued and degraded not to exceed compliance constraints. Ops notified.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Engineering spike: implement lightweight sway accounting API + Console UI prototype. (Owner: eng-allocator)
- Telemetry pipe: ensure per-request token estimation is available end-to-end. (Owner: eng-observability)
- Legal/billing review for premium surge pricing and contract language. (Owner: finance-legal)
- Customer pilot: recruit 3 customers across different segments for beta. (Owner: product-dedicated)

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intentionally pragmatic and mixes product + operational details to get feedback from SRE/allocators/billing. Please annotate sections with comments or ping me in #prod-dedicated.

END OF DRAFT
